posts.name: Uday
posts.cooked:
In the GRPA 3 of week 3, the question asks about the concepts which is going to be taught in week5, so how are we supposed to answer that, as nothing related to that question is taught in week 3’s content.

What they are doing by giving some other weeks content earlier.

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked: The professor did go through the relevant content (albeit not fully) in one of the lecture videos of Week 3. Using that content you’re expected to explore a little bit on your own as well.

posts.name: Uday
posts.cooked:
I didn’t find anything related to that, though found out it by watching the week 5 lecture.

Thanks for ur help.

posts.name: Ishan Shishodiya
posts.cooked: You don’t need to restrict yourself with the course content only. Feel free to use any external sources to learn as well. There are various websites and courses on YouTube which teach fundamentals of bash too.

posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: It can be easily solved without week 5 content. If you know basic shell variables… I think the course never restricts from a little exploring.

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: It is good you are having this revelation now before the quiz/oppe/ET than during – so you can prepare accordingly for them. Because diploma courses (at least system commands) will not hand-hold you to the solutions like a school/board exam. You are expected to go through course content for an introduction to the topic at hand, then you are expected to explore it further on your own. Both in terminal by playing with it and exploring other options, and online and other resources (web, book, etc). This is the same framework followed by all IIT/Ivy League on campus courses as well. “The exact thing was not discussed in lectures” is not an excuse and will not be entertained there, or here. Similarly lectures can focus on introducing topics whereas questions can focus on your critical thinking ability on the topic / how to use it – It wont be a memorization challenge.
